plain_claim: For any theory T, any explicit definition d (a new k-ary function symbol defined by an old term, or a new k-ary relation symbol defined by an old formula) and any model S of T: the structures on S's carrier that keep S's old symbols and satisfy the definitional extension T + d are exactly one structure, the canonical expansion d.expand S.

hypotheses.name: hS : S.ModelsTh T
hypotheses.purpose: Gives that the canonical expansion satisfies the translated axioms of T. Tight; witness class: the inconsistent theory {falsum} over {zero, succ, le} with the standard structure on Nat, where the characterization fails at S' = d.expand S.

nonvacuity_witness: The standard structure on Nat for {zero, succ, le}, the empty theory, and the definition two := succ (succ zero).
non_claims: Uniqueness holds without assuming that S models T (defExt_expansion_unique_of_axiom).
The structures share the carrier with S; nothing is said about expansions up to isomorphism or on other carriers.

Kernel definitional equality of a dependent type theory is not modeled: Defn.theory adds a first-order defining axiom, and Defn.DeltaConv is conversion for one defined symbol over first-order syntax (no beta, iota or eta, no type-level conversion such as Vec a c versus Vec a e).

Recursive definitions (the new symbol occurring in its own definiens), type or inductive definitions, definitions of a function symbol by a formula with a proved unique-existence condition, and polymorphic or overloaded definitions are not modeled.

plain_claim: For a theory T' over L plus one new k-ary function symbol c: if c is explicitly definable in T' (FnExplicitlyDefinable T': some old-language formula theta(y, x) satisfies T' |= forall y x, (c(x) = y <-> theta(y, x))), then any two models S1, S2 of T' on the same carrier whose reducts to L coincide are equal.

hypotheses.name: hdef : FnExplicitlyDefinable T'
hypotheses.purpose: The substantive hypothesis: transparency of c, modeled as explicit definability. Tight; witness class: the language {P} plus a fresh constant c with the single axiom P c, on Bool with P everywhere true, where c = true and c = false are two models with the same reduct.

hypotheses.name: h₁ : S₁.ModelsTh T'
hypotheses.purpose: Assumes S1 is a model of T'. Tight; witness class: {zero, succ, le} on Nat with the definitional extension by two, S1 the expansion interpreting two as 3 and S2 the canonical expansion (the counterexample records both orders).

hypotheses.name: h₂ : S₂.ModelsTh T'
hypotheses.purpose: Assumes S2 is a model of T'. Tight; same witness class with the roles of S1 and S2 exchanged.

hypotheses.name: hred : S₁.reduct (SigHom.inclFn L k) = S₂.reduct (SigHom.inclFn L k)
hypotheses.purpose: Assumes the two models agree on the old symbols. Tight; witness class: {zero, succ, le} on Nat with the definitional extension by two, comparing the canonical expansions of natStr and natStr2.

nonvacuity_witness: The definitional extension of the empty {zero, succ, le}-theory by two is explicitly definable and has a model (take S1 = S2 that model).
non_claims: The converse (uniqueness of expansions implies explicit definability, Beth's theorem) is not proved here.
The theorem is about a new function symbol; the analogue for a new relation symbol is not stated.
Transparency here means explicit definability by a first-order formula of the old language; it is not kernel delta-reduction in a dependent type theory.

WeakSortSpec and StrongSortSpec are higher-order characterizations of a function on List Nat; this first-order theorem does not apply to them, and any analogy to weakSortSpec_admits_natSort_and_weirdSort is informal (not proved here).

Separately proved consequences, which are not part of this theorem's statement: a symbol introduced by an explicit definition is explicitly definable in the definitional extension (defnFn_theory_fnExplicitlyDefinable), and the constant whose sole axiom is P c is not explicitly definable (axPc_not_fnExplicitlyDefinable).

FnExplicitlyDefinable T' holds vacuously when T' has no model on any carrier (fnExplicitlyDefinable_of_no_model; instance: falsum_theory_fnExplicitlyDefinable_no_model); the conclusion is then vacuous as well.

For a satisfiable T', FnExplicitlyDefinable T' gives uniqueness of expansions (S1 = S2), not conservativity or the expansion property over a base theory: singletonDefTheory explicitly defines c and has a model, yet it entails the old-language sentence forall x y, x = y, which the empty {P}-theory does not entail; so it is not Conservative over the empty theory and does not have the ExpansionProperty over it (fnExplicitlyDefinable_satisfiable_not_conservative).

hypotheses.name: hexp : ExpansionProperty ι T T'
hypotheses.purpose: Assumes every model of T expands. Tight; witness class: the language {P} plus a fresh constant c with the axiom P c over the empty theory (a one-point countermodel).

nonvacuity_witness: Adding a fresh 0-ary relation symbol with no axioms to the empty {P}-theory has the expansion property.

plain_claim: A function f : List Nat -> List Nat satisfies StrongSortSpec ('for every list, the output is sorted by <= and is a permutation of the input') iff f = natSort (merge sort). In particular StrongSortSpec determines a function: it has a lawful interpretation, and at most one.
nonvacuity_witness: Merge sort satisfies StrongSortSpec.

plain_claim: For any type a with decidable equality, intended predicate Spec, lists Pos and Neg with correct labels (every element of Pos satisfies Spec and no element of Neg does) and point x0 outside Pos ++ Neg: the two deciders memDecider Pos ('x is in Pos') and memDecider (x0 :: Pos) ('x is x0 or in Pos') both agree with Spec on every example, and at least one of them does not decide Spec.

hypotheses.name: [DecidableEq α]
hypotheses.purpose: Used to form memDecider (decide (x in l)). The deciders are built from the lists and this instance without consulting Spec; they are executable when the supplied instance is computable. Every type has a classical instance, so the hypothesis restricts nothing.

hypotheses.name: hlab : LabelsCorrect Spec Pos Neg
hypotheses.purpose: Used to show that memDecider Pos agrees with Spec on the examples. Tight; witness class: Bool with one mislabeled positive example (Spec = (. = true), Pos = [false], Neg = [], x0 = true). The conclusion can also hold when this hypothesis fails: on Nat with Spec = (. = 0), Pos = Neg = [0] and x0 = 1 the labels are incorrect and the conclusion holds (label_deciders_conclusion_without_hypotheses).

hypotheses.name: hx₀ : x₀ ∉ Pos ++ Neg
hypotheses.purpose: Used to make the two deciders differ at x0. Tight; witness class: Bool exhausted by the examples (Spec = (. = true), Pos = [true], Neg = [false], x0 = true), where both deciders decide Spec. The conclusion can also hold when this hypothesis fails: on Nat with Spec = True, Pos = [0], Neg = [] and x0 = 0 the conclusion holds (label_deciders_conclusion_without_hypotheses).

nonvacuity_witness: Nat, Spec = even, Pos = [0, 2], Neg = [1], x0 = 4.
non_claims: Does not say which of the two deciders is wrong; that depends on Spec x0.

Deciders are Boolean-valued functions; computability is not expressed as a proposition. memDecider Pos is executable when the supplied DecidableEq instance is computable; an instance exists classically for every type, and computability is outside the formal statement.
The deciders are built from the labels alone; deciders that consult further information are not addressed.

hypotheses.purpose: Provides a point outside the examples where d can deviate. Tight; witness class: the finite type Bool with the exhaustive example list [true, false], where every decider agreeing on the examples decides Spec.

hypotheses.purpose: Lets adjacent relatedness propagate along the list. Tight; witness class: r = (!=) on Nat with the three-element list [0, 1, 0].

nonvacuity_witness: <= on Nat is transitive on [1, 2, 2, 3].
non_claims: TransOn r l lets the three elements range independently over the members of l, with repetition and ignoring list positions (so [0, 1] fails TransOn (!=) via 0, 1, 0; ne_not_transOn); a version restricted to positions i < j < k is not stated.
Not necessary for a single list (transOn_not_necessary_for_single_list).

plain_claim: For any signature morphism iota : L -> L', structure S' of L' and formula phi of L: under every assignment, phi read along iota has the same truth value in S' as phi has in the reduct of S' (the old symbols read through iota).
nonvacuity_witness: Expanding a {P}-structure by a constant keeps the old symbols: its reduct is the original structure.
non_claims: Reference point: the same statement as the infrastructure lemma sat_map (structural induction on formulas).
Stability is relative to the reduct: reinterpreting an old symbol can change a truth value (stored_formula_stable_ce_reinterpreted) but need not (reinterpreted_symbol_need_not_flip_truth).

Along the non-injective morphism ιCollapse from {a, b} (two 0-ary relation symbols) to a language with one 0-ary relation symbol, the empty theory over the target language is not Conservative over the empty theory over the source language and does not have the ExpansionProperty over it (noninjective_hom_empty_theories_not_conservative).
Displayed text is not stable under environment extension in the toy elaborator (default_numeral_change_flips_truth, new_coercion_flips_truth, new_instance_flips_truth).

plain_claim: In a toy elaborator from displayed arithmetic comparisons to stored sentences, each of three environment extensions (prepending int as the default numeral type, prepending a coercion nat -> int, prepending an instance making / on int Euclidean) changes the stored reading of an old displayed string from a false sentence to a true one in the intended structure on Int.
nonvacuity_witness: Concrete instances (no hypotheses).
non_claims: Env.elab computes one join type for both sides of a comparison and pushes coercions to numeral leaves, including inside ascribed subterms (so - in (0 : nat) - (1 : nat) < (0 : int) becomes integer subtraction after the coercion is added); Lean 4 elaborates (0 : Nat) - (1 : Nat) at Nat before coercing (not proved here).
A changed elaboration need not change truth (elab_change_without_truth_change).
Notation and name-resolution changes are not modeled.

plain_claim: For any two environments e, e' and finite list D of displayed strings of the toy elaborator: elabPreservesCheck e e' D = true iff every string of D that elaborates under e elaborates to the same stored sentence under e' (ElabPreservesAccepted); and elabInvariantCheck e e' D = true iff every string of D has the same elaboration result, including failure, under e and e' (ElabInvariantOn).
nonvacuity_witness: The default-type change preserves the annotated strings sCoe and sDiv and does not preserve 0 - 1 < 0.
non_claims: Reference point: the checkers are List.all over decidable equality of elaboration results; the theorem is definitional.

ElabInvariantOn is symmetric (elabInvariantOn_symm) and can reject an extension that changes no previously accepted string: adding the coercion nat -> int to a coercion-free environment preserves every accepted string of the whole surface language but is not invariant on [sCoe], which it newly accepts (additive_coercion_preserves_but_not_invariant).
ElabPreservesAccepted ignores strings rejected under e; whether a string is accepted is the separate check (e.elab s).isSome.

Equal stored syntax read under the same interpretations of its symbols has the same truth value (stored_formula_stable_under_expansion, relative to the reduct). Reinterpreting a referenced symbol can change a truth value (stored_formula_stable_ce_reinterpreted) but need not (reinterpreted_symbol_need_not_flip_truth).

plain_claim: For a signature morphism iota : LE -> L, domain knowledge K and a requirement R over LE, and a specification Spec over L: if K u Spec adds no LE-consequence to the translated K (SpecConservative) and K, Spec |= R (Adequate), then the translated K already entails the translated R.

hypotheses.name: hcons : SpecConservative ι K Spec
hypotheses.purpose: The criterion under test. Tight; witness class: a two-symbol propositional base vocabulary {train, car} extended by one symbol gate, with K empty and Spec = {train -> gate, gate -> not car}.

hypotheses.name: hadq : Adequate ι K Spec R
hypotheses.purpose: The requirement argument. Tight; same witness class, with the empty specification.

nonvacuity_witness: Domain knowledge {not (train and car)} with the empty specification is conservative and adequate.
non_claims: Consequence: under SpecConservative, a specification contributes nothing toward a requirement over LE; whenever K, Spec |= R holds, the translated K alone entails the translated R. In the setting with control and visibility, the analogous criterion ConservativeFor rejects the relatively consistent (SpecRelConsistent) and adequate specification of crossing_control_spec_relConsistent_not_envConservative.
The expansion-property criterion collapses in the same way: under SpecExpansionProperty, Adequate holds iff the translated K entails the translated R (specExpansionProperty_adequate_iff).

The conclusion is about the translated K. Reading it back as K |= R follows when the change of vocabulary is itself conservative (Conservative ι K (K.map ι), by the definition of Conservative); without that, the reading can fail: the empty theory over the target language (which has the same models as the translated empty theory) entails a translated sentence that the empty theory over the source language does not, for a fresh constant over empty carriers (fresh_constant_not_conservative_with_empty_carriers) and for a non-injective morphism (noninjective_hom_empty_theories_not_conservative).

This generic setting is not the reference-model split of Gunter et al.: there K and R may mention machine-controlled shared phenomena and the specification uses a smaller vocabulary; see specRelConsistent_adequate_ev_requirement_implies_domain_entails.

plain_claim: In a split LEv -> LS -> LW (machine-visible environment-controlled phenomena, shared phenomena, environment-visible phenomena) with domain knowledge K over LW, a specification Spec over LS and a sentence rho over LEv: if Spec is relatively consistent with K (SpecRelConsistent: for every model M of K, some LS-structure on M's carrier has the same LEv-reduct as M and satisfies Spec, and every such LS-structure is the LS-reduct of some model of K on that carrier) and K, Spec |= rho (rho translated to LW; SpecAdequate), then K |= rho already.

hypotheses.name: hrc : SpecRelConsistent ιVS ιSW K Spec
hypotheses.purpose: The specification condition. Tight; witness class: a propositional split with train and car machine-visible and environment-controlled, gate machine-controlled, no hidden phenomena, K empty and Spec = {train -> gate, gate -> not car}.

hypotheses.name: hadq : SpecAdequate ιSW K Spec ((ρ.map ιVS).map ιSW)
hypotheses.purpose: Specification adequacy. Tight; same witness class with the empty specification.

nonvacuity_witness: Same split with K = {not (train and car)} and the empty specification.
non_claims: The theorem assumes the requirement is a translated LEv-sentence. For a requirement that mentions hidden environment phenomena the conclusion can fail: a relatively consistent specification meets a requirement that K alone does not entail (crossing_control_spec_relConsistent_not_envConservative).

SpecRelConsistent renders formula (5) of Gunter et al. model-theoretically, with all phenomena interpreted over one shared carrier; this correspondence is a modeling bridge (derived), not a kernel-checked fact about their notation.
Time, the machine M and the program P of the reference model are not modeled.

plain_claim: With train environment-controlled and machine-visible, car environment-controlled and hidden, gate machine-controlled, domain knowledge domainA = {gate -> not car} and specification specA = {train -> gate}: the specification meets not (train and car) (SpecAdequate), the domain knowledge alone does not entail it, the specification is relatively consistent (SpecRelConsistent ιVSA ιSWA domainA specA), and domain knowledge plus specification is not consequence-conservative over the domain knowledge for sentences over the environment-controlled vocabulary {train, car} (not ConservativeFor ιEWA domainA (withSpec ιSWA domainA specA)).
nonvacuity_witness: Concrete instance (no hypotheses).
non_claims: One example: it shows that ConservativeFor over the environment-controlled vocabulary fails for a specification that is adequate and SpecRelConsistent; it says nothing about how often this happens. Calling this control legitimate is the reading of SpecRelConsistent as the relative-consistency condition of Gunter et al. (derived, modeling bridge).
Whether gate -> not car is true of a real crossing is a domain assumption of the example, not a proved fact.

Name: 'envConservative' in the theorem name stands for ConservativeFor ιEWA domainA (withSpec ιSWA domainA specA), consequence-conservativity of domain knowledge plus specification over the domain knowledge for sentences over {train, car}. It is neither the generic SpecConservative of the vocabulary-extension setting nor Conservative ι T T' along a signature morphism ι.

plain_claim: With train and car environment-controlled and machine-visible, gate machine-controlled and empty domain knowledge (ιSWB is the identity, so the shared and environment-visible vocabularies coincide): the specification specB = {train -> gate, gate -> not car} meets not (train and car) (SpecAdequate), the empty domain knowledge does not entail not (train and car), and specB does not accept every environment input (not SpecAcceptsEveryEnvInput ιVSB ιSWB Theory.empty specB); moreover, for every specification Spec over these phenomena, if Spec meets not (train and car) with empty domain knowledge, then Spec is not relatively consistent (not SpecRelConsistent ιVSB ιSWB Theory.empty Spec).
nonvacuity_witness: Concrete instance (no hypotheses).
non_claims: The universal part is stated for this setting (car environment-controlled and visible to the machine, empty domain knowledge). In the different setting of crossing_control_spec_relConsistent_not_envConservative (car hidden, domain knowledge gate -> not car), an adequate specification that is SpecRelConsistent exists.
Calling the failure an assumption about the environment is the reading of the relative-consistency condition in Gunter et al.; it is a modeling bridge (derived), not a separate theorem.

Proof detail, not part of the statement: the witness for not SpecAcceptsEveryEnvInput is the one-point model in which train and car both hold; no structure on the shared phenomena with that train and car satisfies specB. The universal part follows from specRelConsistent_adequate_ev_requirement_implies_domain_entails.
